title: Session Export
description: A completed training session exported by AccelerometerLifting for LLM analysis.

schemaVersion.description: 1.1: velocityLoss_pct is best-to-LAST rep; unmeasured phases are null rather than 0; tempo compliance scores movement digits only; repMetricsComplete reports per-rep coverage. 1.2: a set may carry `geometry`, the resolved direction and sensor mounting its numbers were measured with, plus the provenance of each value. Purely additive — no key from 1.1 changed type or stopped being written, so a 1.1 reader works unchanged against a 1.2 export. 1.3: a session may carry `timeZone`, the device's zone and UTC offset when it was recorded. Also purely additive — `startedAt` and `endedAt` are unchanged and still UTC with a `Z` — so a 1.2 reader works unchanged against a 1.3 export. 1.4: a set's `hr` block is published only from the samples the strap's own report supports. `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` are taken over those samples rather than over every sample; `endOfSetBpm` is present only when the set's FINAL sample is one of them, and is never backfilled from an earlier one; and the whole block is absent when the strap reported nothing usable. NOT purely additive: no key changed type or stopped being written, but `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` are computed over a different population and `endOfSetBpm` names a different sample, so a 1.3 reader comparing these figures across versions is comparing different quantities. 1.5: on a body-weight set, `plannedLoad_kg` is paired on the same scale as `load_kg` — the plan's declared added load plus the same body weight, rather than the added load alone. NOT purely additive for the same reason 1.4 was not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE `plannedLoad_kg` carries for a body-weight set changes meaning, so a 1.4 reader comparing it against `load_kg` on such a set is comparing quantities that used to disagree on purpose and now do not. 1.6: a set summary may carry `romSpread_pct`, how far the reps of the set disagree with each other about `rom_m`, as a percentage of `meanRom_m`. Purely additive - no key from 1.5 changed type or stopped being written, so a 1.5 reader works unchanged against a 1.6 export. 1.7: a set's `hr` block may carry `minBpm`, the lowest bpm its trusted samples support — the same population `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` already draw from. Purely additive — no existing key changes type or stops being written, so a 1.6 reader works unchanged against a 1.7 export. Computed at export time from the set's own raw HRM stream rather than a stored column, so it is available on every session already recorded, not only ones captured after this version shipped. 1.8: `hrvRmssd_ms` is computed from a de-duplicated R-R series. This strap re-sends its last completed interval at a fixed ~500 ms cadence whenever no new beat has arrived, and every repeat contributed a successive difference of exactly zero; a notification identical to its predecessor is now counted once. NOT purely additive: no key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE is computed over a different population, so a 1.7 reader comparing this figure across versions is comparing different quantities. On the one worn capture held here the value rises from 11.12 to 12.20 -- +9.7% measured against the OLD value, equivalently 8.8% of the new one -- where those figures are Hrv.rmssdMs over that session's seventeen persisted set streams concatenated into one series. The effect is larger the lower the heart rate, because the re-sent fraction rises as the beat interval lengthens against a fixed cadence. Recorded here because it is not the first such change: #27 altered the same field by about -11% on the same corpus WITHOUT a version bump, which was an error this entry corrects forward rather than repeats. 1.9: a set's `hr` block is published only when the set's own R-R intervals account for at least a third of the time the set covers. A strap that has lost contact holds its last interval and re-sends it, so its intervals cover a fraction of the elapsed time while a worn strap's tile it; a stream that cannot show it was tracking a heart now publishes no `avgBpm`, `maxBpm`, `minBpm` or `endOfSetBpm` rather than a believable resting figure. A stream carrying no R-R intervals at all is NOT affected: it cannot produce this measure, and absence of evidence is not silenced here. This applies RETROACTIVELY to sessions already recorded, which is most of its effect: `avgBpm`, `maxBpm` and `endOfSetBpm` are stored when a set is recorded, so the export re-asks the question of the set's stored raw stream and withholds the whole `hr` block or none of it. A set whose raw stream is no longer stored cannot be re-judged and is published exactly as before. Note for readers comparing sets: an `hr` block carrying `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` but no `minBpm` means the raw stream was unavailable to compute a minimum from -- it is a statement about the archive, NOT a statement that the heart rate never went low. The session-level `heartRate` block is withheld when a session has sets and none of them publishes an `hr` block, because that block is aggregated from the set rows and must not outlive them. NOT purely additive, for the reason 1.4 was not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the population these figures are computed over changes, so a 1.8 reader comparing them across versions is comparing different quantities. 1.10: `velocityLoss_pct` is withheld, rather than published as 0.0, when the last rep the sensor resolved is also the fastest of the set. The figure is best rep to LAST rep, so its reference is a maximum taken over a list that contains its own last element: `best - last` can never be negative, and the quotient reaches exactly 0.0 only when the last rep ties the maximum. A last rep that ties the maximum is also the signature of a spurious final detection -- the sensor being set down, or the lifter getting off the machine, moving faster than any rep -- so the reassuring reading and the artefact could not be told apart. A new key `velocityLossBasis` names which case a set is in, and is present whenever the set resolved any reps at all -- including, and especially, when the figure itself is absent, so that a WITHHELD figure is distinguishable from one an older app version never wrote. NOT purely additive: `velocityLoss_pct` STOPS BEING WRITTEN on sets where 1.9 wrote it, so a 1.9 reader treating a present number as authoritative now finds an absent key rather than a changed value. Applies RETROACTIVELY to sessions already recorded, which is most of its effect: the judgement is re-derived at export time from the set's stored reps rather than read from the stored scalar, the same way 1.9 re-asks its question of the stored raw stream. A genuinely flat set -- one where the lifter really did hold velocity to the last rep -- is withheld too. That is a decision, not an oversight: best-to-last with last equal to best is the degenerate case of the definition and carries no information about fatigue in either direction, and `velocityLossBasis` still reports that the last rep was the fastest. Note for readers parsing this field numerically: the string "1.10" is not the number 1.1 -- float("1.10") collides with schema version 1.1, which is a different contract. Compare it as a string. 1.11: a set may carry `plannedPrep_s` and `prep_s`. Purely additive: no key from 1.10 changed type or stopped being written, so a 1.10 reader works unchanged against a 1.11 export. Both keys are absent on a set that played no prep and on every set recorded before this version. 1.12: a set's per-rep figures cover only the detections whose drive began at or before the set's own `Done` cue. A guided set goes on recording after the metronome stops prescribing: the eleven sets of session 32 that carry both a `Done` cue and an IMU stream keep recording for 4.3 to 13.7 s past it, measured as last sample minus cue. The sensor being put down, unclipped or carried in that window segments as a rep like any other. Those detections are excluded before anything is derived from the rep list, so `repMetrics`, `velocityLoss_pct`, `velocityLossBasis`, `repMetricsComplete`, `reps` on a sensor-counted set and every field of `summary` are computed over a different population of reps. NOT purely additive, for the reason 1.4, 1.8 and 1.9 were not: no key changes type or stops being written, but a 1.11 reader comparing these figures across versions is comparing different quantities. Measured sizes: on the session that found it, set 6's `velocityLoss_pct` moves from 82.6 to 52.1; on three captures of an earlier session, `summary.peakConVel_mps` falls from 1.673 to 0.737, from 1.707 to 0.768 and from 1.261 to 0.910 m/s, and those same three move from `velocityLossBasis` "terminalRepIsFastest" to "measured" -- they were withheld because nothing in the rep list could separate a spurious final detection from a set held flat to the end, and the cue track answers that from outside the rep list. The basis vocabulary itself is unchanged. A set all of whose detections began after the cue publishes no `velocityLossBasis`, which qualifies 1.10's promise that the key is present whenever the set resolved any reps. The boundary is the cue's own timestamp rather than the end of its utterance, which is recorded nowhere, and a detection that straddles the boundary is kept: what makes a movement a rep of the set is that the lifter began it while the set was running. A set whose cue track never says `Done` is not bounded at all and no boundary is invented for it -- an ad-hoc set recorded with the voice guide off, every set recorded before the app wrote cue tracks, and any guided set the lifter ended before the prescription was called through, which is five of the seventeen sets of the session this was measured on. This does not apply retroactively: the exporter re-derives these figures from the STORED rep list, and a stored rep carries durations, velocities, a range and an ordinal index -- an index into the rep list, not into the samples -- but no instant, so an already-recorded row cannot be placed against its own cue track without re-running segmentation over its stored raw IMU stream, which the exporter does not do. Sets recorded before this version publish exactly what they published before. 1.13: `duration_s` on a timed set is the figure the set was RECORDED with, not the seconds its clock measured. A hold or carry now ends when its clock reaches the seconds the set was WORKING TO -- `plannedDuration_s` unless the lifter changed the hold in the change-set dialog, in which case theirs -- so a set that ran to its target publishes `plannedDuration_s` only when the lifter did not change it; a set the lifter ended by hand publishes what it lasted; a set corrected afterwards on the rest screen publishes the corrected figure. NOT purely additive, for the reason 1.4, 1.5, 1.8, 1.9 and 1.12 were not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE `duration_s` carries changes for the majority case -- under auto-end that is every timed set the lifter does not cut short -- so a 1.12 reader comparing hold seconds across versions is comparing different quantities. What a 1.12 reader may assume and a 1.13 reader may not: that `duration_s` is a measurement of elapsed time, and that `duration_s == plannedDuration_s` is evidence the lifter stopped on the word. What changes in the other direction: under 1.12 a timed set ran until the lifter ended it by hand, so a recorded figure above `plannedDuration_s` was the ordinary case and carried the walk back to the phone inside it. Under 1.13 it is no longer the ordinary case, but it is NOT excluded. A set the lifter ends by hand still publishes what its clock measured, and the tick loop counts one-second delays rather than wall-clock seconds, so a hand-ended set can publish more seconds than were prescribed with no rest-screen correction applied. A `duration_s` above `plannedDuration_s` is therefore not evidence of a stated overage. Corrected and measured seconds are NOT distinguishable in either version: reps publish `repsManual` and there is no counterpart for duration, so a stated figure and a measured one are the same key. This does NOT apply retroactively: `duration_s` is read from the stored `actualDurationS` column rather than re-derived at export time, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly what it published before, and what changes is which quantity a newly recorded set stores there. No size is stated for the shift: how much of a pre-1.13 hold was phone-retrieval time is a question only a real session answers, and this repository holds no capture of a timed set to measure it from. 1.13 carries a SECOND change, and it is additive where the first is not: a set may carry `repMarks`, the epoch-ms instants at which a rep was counted -- the lifter's taps on a manually counted set, the voice guide's calls on a guided one. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, so a reader that ignores `repMarks` reads a 1.13 export exactly as it read a 1.12 one; the `duration_s` warning above is the half of this version that a 1.12 reader must be re-checked against, and this half is not. Two changes share one version because 1.13 was unreleased when the second landed, and minting 1.14 for a key no reader had shipped against would publish a boundary that never existed. `repMarks` is absent, never an empty array, on every set that counted nothing out loud -- which includes every ordinary sensor-counted set and every set recorded before the app stored marks, and those two are not distinguishable from each other. Its length may disagree with `reps`: a rest-screen correction rewrites the count and cannot reach a mark already written, and the guide calls a rep on its own schedule whether or not the lifter followed it. 1.13 carries a THIRD change, additive on the same terms and under the same version for the same reason (#156): a set may carry `sensors`, saying how many accelerometers it was armed with, which roles they carried, which of those reached the raw archive and which one the set's figures came from. What each field means is stated once, at $defs.setSensors. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, and it is ABSENT on every ordinary one-sensor set -- so a single-sensor export is byte-for-byte what 1.12 wrote apart from the version string itself, which is written unconditionally and therefore cannot be held identical under any bump at all. In the raw archive the same set gains one CSV per role, named with the role appended to the kind (set01_bench_press_imu-a.csv), and meta.json carries the role-to-file mapping with a per-stream sample count and a rate measured from that stream; a one-sensor set's CSV keeps the name it has always had. 1.13 carries a FOURTH change, additive on the same terms and under the same version for the same reason (#159): a session may carry `sessionRpe`, the lifter's own 1-10 answer to how the whole workout felt, stated once when they finished it. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, and it is ABSENT on every session the lifter did not rate as well as on every session recorded before this version -- absence means unrated and must not be read as a low rating. What each field means is stated once, at the property itself, including the warning that matters most for this one: `sessionRpe` and a set's `rpe` are two different instruments whose published ranges overlap, and nothing but their descriptions tells them apart. 1.13 carries a FIFTH change, under the same unreleased version for the same reason, and this one is NOT additive (#176): `voiceCues` records the rep call the guide MERGES into a stroke's own word, which until now was spoken and written nowhere. Where a rep call has no pause to sit in, the guide says the stroke word and the call as a single utterance -- `Down, Rep 3` -- because the speech engine cancels whatever it was saying when a new utterance arrives; only the stroke word reached the cue track, so on those plans the array named no rep at all. Measured on the session that found it, 16 sets on app 0.1.43: `Rep N` and `Last rep` appear ZERO times in 539 cue rows, on a session where the lifter heard a rep call on every rep after each set's first -- 157 calls spoken and unwritten. They were datable at all only because a carrying stroke gives up its first tempo count to make room for the call, leaving a hole where a `1` should have been: exactly one `1` per set, on all sixteen. What changes for a reader: a newly recorded set's `voiceCues` carries `Rep N` and `Last rep` rows it did not carry before, and the stroke row keeps its own value and gains a SECOND row at the SAME `t_ms` rather than being renamed. A consumer counting or matching stroke rows is unaffected; a consumer counting ALL rows, or assuming one instant is one row, sees a different population. That is the reason this is filed as non-additive and not additive -- no key changes type or stops being written, and the contents of an existing array change, which is the shape 1.4, 1.8, 1.9 and 1.12 each carry. This does NOT apply retroactively: cue rows are stored as they are spoken, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly the rows it published before, and nothing in a row distinguishes a set that never spoke a call from one that spoke it and did not write it down. The same change decides where `Last rep` is not spoken at all (#173), and a reader needs both halves or the absence is unreadable: on a schedule whose only slot for the warning is the beat the rep ends on, the guide would be warning about a rep with only one stroke of it left, so it says nothing and the terminal `Done` carries the ending alone. The absence of a Last rep row on such a set is therefore a DECISION and not a gap -- which matters because before this version the same absence meant the opposite, a warning spoken and written nowhere, and the two leave identical evidence. Which schedules those are is not readable from the tempo string: the same four digits put the call at the start of the rep on one lift and at its end on another, and a session recorded both. The finished-rep `Rep N` calls are unaffected and still appear on every such set; what a suppressed warning gives back is the tempo count the carrying stroke had given up for it, so the second that used to be silent carries a digit. 1.13 carries a SIXTH change, under the same unreleased version for the same reason, and it is NOT additive (#157, #174): `plannedReps` and `plannedDuration_s` publish what the PLAN declared, frozen at import, rather than what the lifter left in the change-set dialog's box. Until this version a lifter who dropped a set from 8 to 6 exported plannedReps 6, so no deviation was visible at all; the same set now exports plannedReps 8 beside reps 6. No key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE both keys carry changes on every set the lifter edited, so a reader comparing a planned figure against a performed one across versions is comparing different quantities. This does NOT apply retroactively: both are read from stored columns, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly what it published before. What the lifter STATED -- which after #174 may be a count carried from an earlier set of the block -- is still not exported: a reader sees what was prescribed and what was performed, not what was declared in between, which is #157's remaining half. 1.13 carries a SEVENTH change, additive on the same terms and under the same version for the same reason (#177): a set may carry `added`, saying the LIFTER appended it to the exercise mid-session rather than the plan prescribing it. The control sits with the other between-sets decisions, on the rest screen and on READY, and it is repeatable -- adding two sets is adding one twice. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, and it is ABSENT on every prescribed set and on every set recorded before database v12, so a reader that ignores `added` reads a 1.13 export exactly as it read a 1.12 one. What each field means is stated once, at the property itself, including the two warnings that matter most: an appended set publishes no `plannedLoad_kg`, `plannedReps` or `plannedDuration_s` because nothing prescribed it, but DOES publish `tempoPrescribed`, `rest_s` and `plannedPrep_s` carried unchanged from the rest of the block, and an absent flag on a session recorded before v12 means "prescribed, or recorded before the app could tell" rather than "prescribed". REMOVING a set is not part of this change and no key says a prescribed set was dropped; a plan's remaining sets going unrecorded is what it always was, an absence. SEVEN CHANGES UNDER ONE VERSION is what an unreleased version number is for, and the count is not itself the warning: exactly three of the seven -- `duration_s`, `voiceCues` and the `plannedReps` / `plannedDuration_s` pair -- are not additive, and a 1.12 reader must be re-checked against those three and need not be re-checked against `repMarks`, `sensors`, `sessionRpe` or `added`. 1.14: a RELEASED boundary, not another change under an open number -- 1.13 shipped in v0.1.44, read at the tag. `warmup` is now a PLAN DECLARATION and no longer a rating. Until this version the only thing that could set it was an effort tile the lifter tapped, and that tile stored `warmup: true` together with `rpe: null`, so the effort of every warm-up set was discarded by construction. From 1.14 the plan declares it, through the plan-schema 1.9 key of the same name, and a warm-up set carries a real `rpe` like any other set -- the empty-bar ramp set of a 500 lb squatter is a warm-up by PURPOSE, and what it felt like is a separate fact worth keeping. NOT purely additive: no key changes type or stops being written, but the published description of `warmup` stops telling a reader to exclude these sets from effort analysis, because after this version that instruction is false. A reader that excludes them from VOLUME or progression is unaffected and the field still supports that. This does NOT apply retroactively: `warmup` is read from a stored column, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly what it published before -- and on those sessions `warmup: true` with no `rpe` means the app could not record both, NOT that the lifter declined to rate the set. One consequence to read carefully: a set the lifter added mid-session, and any ad-hoc set, publishes no `warmup` at all even when it was a ramp, because nothing declared it and the app offers no control that says so. 1.14 carries a SECOND change, under the same number because 1.14 is unreleased and the two are one design (#187), and it is NOT additive either: `rpe` is a 1-to-10 scale whose rungs are ANCHORED DIFFERENTLY ALONG ITS LENGTH. 7 to 10 stay reps in reserve -- 3, 2, 1, none left -- and below them the anchors are load headroom: 6 is 'could have added one equipment increment', 4 is two increments, 1 is much more. On a hold or a carry the same three rungs ask in SECONDS instead, because load headroom is meaningless on a plank. The reason the low end stopped being a rep count is measured rather than stylistic: mean error in calling one's own reps in reserve is 2.05 reps at 1 RIR and 5.15 reps at 5 RIR (Zourdos et al., 2019), so at that distance the error is larger than the claim, while a load figure there is answerable and checkable next session. 2, 3 and 5 are valid values that carry NO tile: the gaps exist so the anchors sort, and a reader meeting one is looking at a real value on the same ruler rather than corrupt data. NOT additive and NOT retroactive: no key changes type or stops being written and no stored value is rewritten, but a newly written low value means something the old scale could not say. THE VALUE TO READ CAREFULLY IS 6. Under 1.13 and earlier the grid offered 6 to 10 only, and 6 was its FLOOR, 'easy, 4+ reps left' -- so it absorbed everything the new 1 and 4 now take, and 46% of this lifter's historical ratings sit on it. It is reused rather than retired to 5 because the standard RPE-to-RIR chart puts 6 at 4 RIR, roughly the state 'could have added one increment' describes, so old values stay interpretable on the same ruler; do not read a pre-1.14 6 as specifically meaning one increment. 7 through 10 are unchanged in meaning across this boundary. The warm-up tile is also gone from that grid, which is the first change above. 1.14 carries a THIRD change, additive, under the same number and for the reason the first two share -- worth restating because it was asked for as 1.15: 1.14 was UNRELEASED WHEN THAT WAS WRITTEN and is not now: v0.1.45 shipped it, read at tag c44f1c531d6343d0071f82c062344e7f4eff950f. The sentence was true of v0.1.44, which shipped 1.13 at tag 7cf6e8c3cc546ab8d64c9fb2be86de2129250b43, and it stopped being true when the next tag was cut. The changes below rode under one number on the strength of it, correctly at the time; that window is closed -- the same rule seven changes rode under 1.13 for. The change (#189): a set may carry `limiter`, why it ended, from a closed vocabulary; and `limiterNote`, the lifter's own words where that answer is `other`. No key from 1.13 changes type or stops being written, and both are absent on every set nobody was asked about and on every set recorded before database v13. A 1.13 reader works unchanged against a 1.14 export for this change. 1.14 carries a FOURTH change (#194), under the same unreleased number and NOT additive: `warmup` gains a SECOND PRODUCER. Until now the plan declared it and nothing else could; the lifter may now mark or unmark a set on the rest screen, and where the two disagree the lifter's mark wins. No key changes type and no stored value is rewritten, but a 1.13 reader that treats `warmup: true` as 'the plan said so' must be re-checked, which is why this is flagged rather than filed beside the additive changes. The new key `warmupByLifter` says which of the two a given set carries and is absent on every set the lifter never marked, which is every set recorded before database v13. It does NOT publish the plan's overridden declaration: where the mark disagrees, this document carries the answer and its author, and the app's row keeps both. 1.15: `plannedCount` is REMOVED from a set's `sensors` block and `shortfall` is added to it. NOT additive: a reader that requires plannedCount must be changed. The key said how many accelerometers the PLAN prescribed, and no plan prescribes any -- the app records from whatever is connected, one bar sensor writing one stream and two connected units labelled A and B writing two, on every set of every exercise. A key that kept emitting the old default of 1 would tell a reader a coach intended something. `shortfall` carries what the pair used to carry between plannedCount and `count`: "rolesUnassigned" or "rolesCollide", present only when two units were PAIRED and the app could not tell them apart and therefore recorded one stream. The app never opened a link to the second unit in this state, so this says two units are paired and cannot be told apart -- not that both were powered on or in range. That is the distinction this document must keep making, because "there was one sensor" and "there were two and one was unusable" are different facts about a session. The raw archive's meta.json moves with it: `sensorsPlanned` is gone and `sensorsShortfall` is added, carrying the same two words. Exports declaring 1.13 or 1.14 carry plannedCount inside this block; 1.12 and earlier have no sensors block at all, and even at 1.13 and 1.14 only sets that carried a declaration have one. A reader meeting the key should read it as what a plan asked for under a rule that no longer applies. A NOTE ON THIS DOCUMENT ITSELF, true from 1.15 and not before: this schema describes the CURRENT shape only, and 1.15 is the first version to REMOVE a key rather than add one, so a document declaring an earlier version from the enum above is not thereby valid against this file -- a genuine 1.14 export carrying a set's `sensors` block fails here on `plannedCount`, because `setSensors` sets `additionalProperties` false and no longer declares that key. Validate a pre-1.15 export against the copy of this schema published at its own release tag. The enum lists which versions the APP accepts, not which documents this file validates. 1.16: `bottomPause_s` and `topPause_s` measure the turnaround INSIDE a rep, and exactly one of them is published per rep instead of both. NOT additive and this is the version to re-check a reader against: both keys were REQUIRED under 1.15 and neither is now, and the one that is still written carries a different quantity on some lifts than it did. The key that stops being written is whichever end the rep's own BOUNDARY falls on -- `topPause_s` on a lift whose reps start at the top, `bottomPause_s` on a lift whose reps start at the bottom -- because the stillness at that end is not inside the rep at all: it runs from the end of the rep's last detected phase until the next drive begins, so it holds the lifter's rest and nothing in the segmentation separates a hold from a rest. That is what it was publishing. Measured on the capture this was found on, a single-leg press prescribing NO bottom pause published bottomPause_s of 0.02 / 0.10 / 1.57 / 0.33 / 1.29 / 0.06 / 0.08 / 0.01 s, and issue #93 reports the same field reaching 22.73 s on a leg press with a mean of 1.34 s against a median of 0.16 s. The key that IS still written is unchanged in value on every rep that resolved both its phases; it changes only in that it is absent, rather than 0.0, on a rep the segmenter counted from the drive alone, which has one phase and therefore no turnaround. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated because the headline figure in #93 survives it: the published pause is bounded by the two phases THIS REP resolved, so where segmentation merged reps it spans everything between them. One committed leg-press capture resolves 2 detections for 8 performed reps and its second detection carries a 14.27 s turnaround, which is a true statement about that detection and a useless one about the lifter. Read a pause beside the length of `repMetrics` against `reps`; a set whose detections are far under its rep count has pauses that cover the reps it missed. DOES NOT APPLY RETROACTIVELY, and the boundary is when a set was RECORDED rather than when it was exported. `repMetrics` is built at export time, but from the analysis frozen into the set's row when the set was recorded, and that analysis is what decides which pause a rep carries. So a document declaring 1.16 still carries BOTH keys on every rep it publishes from a set recorded before this version, with the old quantities in them -- the numbers this change exists to stop publishing. Read a rep carrying both keys as pre-1.16 data whatever the document's `schemaVersion` says, and do not compare its two figures with each other or with a post-1.16 rep's single one. 1.16 carries a SECOND change (#141): a guided set that ends without the guide having called `Done` now speaks and records a terminal cue, `Set ended`. That is a set the lifter ended early AND a guided set given no rep target, which the guide never finishes on its own and which therefore completes normally carrying this word. NOT additive, for the reason 1.4, 1.8, 1.9, 1.12 and the 1.13 `voiceCues` change were not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the contents of an existing array change -- a newly recorded guided set with no `Done` on its track carries one row it did not carry before, and a reader matching only `Done` to find the end of a set now misses that ending. This qualifies 1.12's own list of the cases it leaves unbounded: its third member, a guided set the lifter ended before the prescription was called through, no longer occurs from this version, and the other two -- an ad-hoc set recorded with the voice guide off, and every set recorded before the app wrote cue tracks -- are unchanged. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE, said plainly because the issue that asked for it assumed otherwise: it does not tighten anybody's rep list. The tap that ends a set is the tap that stops the recording, so no sample and therefore no detection can lie past the boundary and none is excluded by it. Measured on the session that found this (17 sets, app 0.1.41): the eleven completed sets keep recording 4.3 to 13.7 s past `Done`, while the five the lifter failed stop 0.482 to 0.832 s after their last spoken cue. What changes for a reader is that such a set stops being an ABSENCE -- the derived count of detections beginning after the set was called over moves from a statement that nothing said when the set ended to a measured zero, and an analysis that had to exclude the failed sets no longer does.
