What DOES move for such a reader is the VALUE of summary, velocityLoss_pct, velocityLossBasis, repMetrics and repMetricsComplete on a set carrying a non-zero count, and these two keys are how it can tell. It does NOT apply retroactively, for the 1.18 fourth change's reason: the value is frozen into the stored analysis when the set is analysed, so every set recorded before this number ships carries neither key, permanently.

startedAt.description: When the session's first recorded set began, as a UTC instant. Always UTC with a `Z` designator, in every schema version. This is the unambiguous moment; `timeZone` is what turns it into a local time of day.

endedAt.description: When the session was closed, as a UTC instant. Same rendering rules as `startedAt`.

timeZone.description: The device's time zone and UTC offset at the moment this session was recorded. Absent means the session predates the app capturing it, which is permanent for those sessions — no artifact records the offset a past session was on, and it is deliberately NOT filled in from the exporting device's current zone, which would be right most of the time and silently wrong after a change of zone. Both members are present or the whole object is absent; there is no half-stated form.

id.description: The zone id the device reported, normally an IANA name such as `America/New_York`. Not guaranteed to be one: a device may report a fixed-offset id like `GMT+05:00`, which yields an offset but names no place. Use it to re-derive the offset at any other instant in the session (this matters only if the session ran across a daylight-saving transition); do not assume it identifies a location.

utcOffsetMinutes.description: Minutes east of UTC in effect at `startedAt`, negative west of it; -240 is US Eastern daylight time. Minutes, not hours, because India (+05:30), Nepal (+05:45) and the Chatham Islands (+12:45) are not whole hours. 0 is a real value — London in winter — and is always written, never omitted as a default. Bounds are the ISO 8601 limits of ±18:00, which are wider than any zone in use.

sessionRpe.description: SESSION RPE on a 1-10 scale: how the whole workout felt to the lifter, stated once by them when they finished it. 1 is a session that barely touched them, 10 is one that took everything. THIS IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT FROM THE PER-SET `rpe` AND THE TWO MUST NEVER BE AVERAGED OR COMPARED AS ONE QUANTITY: a set's `rpe` is how much that ONE set had left in it -- reps-in-reserve at 7-10, load or time headroom below -- and is a statement about one set's proximity to failure; this is the whole session on 1-10, and there are no reps left in a session. The two ranges are identical, so nothing but these descriptions tells a reader which scale a given integer is on. ABSENT MEANS UNRATED, WHICH IS NOT A LOW RATING. The rating is skippable with one tap and a lifter who skips it records no answer; every session recorded before this version is absent for the different reason that the app could not ask; the two are not distinguishable here and both mean the lifter never said. Do not substitute a default, a midpoint or an estimate for an absent value. Where it IS present it is ground truth rather than a proxy: a reader can already estimate session effort by aggregating set RPEs, and this is the lifter's own answer, so prefer it over any such estimate. Not measured, not derived, and not comparable between lifters -- it is one person's report of their own session.

hrvRmssd_ms.description: Session-wide HRV (RMSSD, ms) computed from R-R intervals with artifact rejection.

load_kg.description: The load the set is recorded at, body-weight-inclusive on a bodyweight movement. A load corrected on the rest screen after the set is indistinguishable here from one entered before it -- both are the lifter stating what was on the bar -- and the deviation from plannedLoad_kg is what a reader asks. The analysis figures under summary are NOT recomputed on a correction.

load_lb.description: Same load in pounds for convenience; load_kg is canonical.

plannedLoad_kg.description: Present when the set deviated from or followed a plan.

bodyWeight_kg.description: The body weight load_kg was computed with, kilograms, frozen when the set was written (schema 1.19). On body-weight work the recorded load is this plus the added load, which may be NEGATIVE for band or machine assistance, so this is usually the largest term in load_kg and the added or assisting load is load_kg - bodyWeight_kg - exact to within double rounding, not bit-exactly. It is the figure the arithmetic used at the time, not the lifter's weight today: the app stores one body weight and it moves. ABSENT, never 0, and three states share the absence: loaded work, which has no body in the load path and is readable from geometry.bodyweight beside it; a set recorded before this shipped, which no build stored; and a body-weight set recorded while the app held no body weight at all, whose body-weight term was 0 kg. The last two cannot be told apart here. A published 0 would read as a lifter with no mass.

plannedPrep_s.description: The prep the PLAN prescribed before this set, in whole seconds. This is the exercise's declared prep_s where the plan declared one, and the app's default where it did not or where the set was recorded without a plan at all -- present either way, because a reader holding prep_s alone cannot tell an adjustment from a declaration. Absent when the set played no prep.

prep_s.description: The prep that played before this set, in whole seconds. Whenever it differs from plannedPrep_s, the lifter adjusted the prep for this exercise in the app; they are equal both when no adjustment exists and when the adjustment happens to equal what the plan prescribed. A plan authored from this export should take prep_s rather than re-guess. 0 is a value, not an absence: it is the prep in which nothing is spoken before the set begins. Absent when the set played no prep. FROM 1.18 THIS KEY IS ABSENT on a set that ended before its work phase began: it carries the prep the app SET OUT to play rather than the prep that elapsed, and on such a set the two provably differ. Read `plannedPrep_s` for the prescription; the raw archive's set descriptor carries the set's own start and end instants, which bound how long the cut-off lead-in actually ran. A set recorded before database v15 carries no answer either way and publishes this key exactly as it always did.

rest_s.description: The rest PRESCRIBED after this set, in whole seconds. Never a measurement of how long the lifter actually rested (#76). From 1.19 the instant it is counted FROM is published rather than left to be inferred: the rest starts when the set was CALLED OVER -- the terminal voice cue on the set's own cue track, which the raw archive carries as that set's `cues` file -- and on a set nothing called over, at the set's own end instant, which is every hold and every set recorded with the voice off. The countdown the lifter watches and the archive's `rest_before_hrm` stream -- the rest window, written onto the NEXT set -- both begin at that instant, so the two can be joined. The same instant seeds `rest_after_hrm`, the window a session close writes onto the LAST set when there is no next set to carry it forward. Before 1.19 that stream began instead when the set's capture stopped, which on a guided set that spoke `Done` and kept recording was up to 53.06 s later, measured on one field session's thirteen sets; sets that ended at their terminal cue diverged by nothing. The stream may therefore open with samples that also appear in this set's own `hrm` stream: the capture is copied forward, never moved, so every figure computed over `hrm` -- `hr.avgBpm`, `hr.maxBpm`, `hr.endOfSetBpm` -- is unchanged. The stream is NOT continuous from that instant: `endSet` cancels the in-set collector and the app does not enter its rest stage until the set's row is written, so a heart-rate notification landing in that interval reaches neither capture -- 0.08 to 0.58 s on the one session measured. This gap is unmarked in the archive; do not assume uniform coverage across it. A session recorded by an earlier build carries the old window and cannot be corrected, because nothing stored the two instants apart.

scoredPhases.description: Which phases were scored. Pauses are measured and reported but never scored.

actualEccConRatio.description: Measured eccentric:concentric contrast, over the reps that resolved both phases. Reps counted on the drive alone are excluded from both means, so this need not cover every rep of the set.

velocityLoss_pct.description: Best rep to LAST rep, percent -- the drawdown at the point the set was stopped. Absent whenever there is no such figure; `velocityLossBasis` says which case the set is in. A published 0.0 is still possible and means a loss below 0.05 percent, rounded to one decimal; it does not mean the last rep tied the fastest, which is the case that withholds the key instead.

velocityLossBasis.description: Which case `velocityLoss_pct` is in. "measured": the figure is present. "notEnoughReps": fewer than two reps were resolved, so there was no pair to take a difference over. "noReference": no rep carried a positive drive velocity to divide by. "terminalRepIsFastest": the last rep resolved was the fastest of the set, which makes best-to-last exactly zero by construction and says nothing about fatigue -- the figure is withheld rather than published as 0.0, and this is also what a detection after the set ended looks like. Present whenever the set resolved any reps, including when `velocityLoss_pct` is absent; absent only when no reps were resolved at all, the same condition under which `repMetricsComplete` is absent.

refusedDetections.description: How many detections the analyzer judged were NOT reps of this set, removing them from the list every other figure here is computed over - schema 1.19, issue #125. The rule: a detection that resolved no eccentric partner AND whose rom_m exceeds 4.5x the median rom_m of the set's other detections is not a rep. The bound is relative to the set's own reps rather than absolute, because the equipment's travel does not change within a set and an absolute range bound would need a figure per exercise. ABSENT, 0 and a positive number are three different facts. Absent: fewer than four detections resolved, so no median of others existed to derive a bound from - or the set was recorded before this version, which is permanent, because the value is frozen into the stored analysis when the set is analysed and nothing re-runs the segmenter at export time. 0: a bound was derived and refused nothing. Positive: that many detections were removed. THIS IS NOT A COUNT OF THE SET'S PHANTOMS. The bound is fitted to the app's committed capture corpus and is placed to err toward admitting a bad detection rather than refusing a real rep - a refused real rep would move velocityLoss_pct, which is best rep to LAST rep, against the wrong rep. The eccentric-partner clause is not decoration: the corpus holds a two-phase detection ABOVE the bound, and that clause is the only thing keeping it. A 0 means nothing was far enough out to refuse, never that the set's figures are sound. NOTHING IS DELETED: the set's raw IMU stream is published unchanged and any refused detection can be re-derived from it.

refusedDetectionReason.description: Why refusedDetections is non-zero, and absent whenever that key is absent or 0. "unpairedRangeOutlier": a detection with no eccentric partner whose range is an outlier against the set's own reps. Named for both clauses on purpose - a paired detection at the same range is kept, so this is not a range cap.

hr.description: Heart rate for this set, summarised over the samples the strap's own report supports. Absent when the strap reported nothing usable, and equally absent when no strap was connected -- the two cannot be told apart from this document, and the raw per-set HRM CSV in the accompanying archive is the only place the difference is visible.

endOfSetBpm.description: Heart rate at the LAST sample of the set, present only when that sample is itself usable. Never backfilled from an earlier sample: this key names a time as much as a value.

minBpm.description: The lowest heart rate this set's trusted samples support -- the same population avgBpm and maxBpm are drawn from, never the whole stream. Present only when at least one sample is trusted; never zero, which would read as a measurement rather than nothing to measure.

repMetrics.description: Per-rep detail; present only in detailed exports.

voiceCues.description: Spoken voice cues during the set ('Down', 'Hold', 'Up', 'Drive', 'Return', '3', 'Ready', 'Brace', 'Rep 4', 'Last rep', 'Done', 'Set ended', 'Time'...), stamped in epoch ms on the same clock as the raw IMU/HR streams so they can be cross-referenced with accelerometer data. Detailed export only. A bare digit is a TEMPO COUNT -- the guide counting a stroke out second by second, or a timed set counting down -- and never a rep number; a rep is always named in full, as 'Rep 4' or as 'Last rep'. From 1.19 a guided call names the rep the guide is calling for -- 'Rep 4' as the fourth rep falls due, and 'Last rep' for the final one, which is why no guided set says 'Rep N' for its planned N; before 1.19 the same call counted FINISHED reps, so a 'Rep 4' row named the rep behind the one being lifted and 'Last rep' fell on the rep before the last. WHEN a call is heard depends on the schedule and is not uniform: on the two schedules that merge the call into a stroke it is spoken during the rep it names, and on the schedule whose prescription ends in a pause it is spoken in the previous rep's closing pause, before the rep it names has begun. That holds for 'Last rep' exactly as it does for a number. Which schedule a set used is not readable from the tempo string alone. The UNGUIDED counter runs on a different clock and is unchanged either side of 1.19: it speaks as a rep completes, so its 'Rep N' counts finished reps and its 'Last rep' lands as rep N-1 completes. Nothing in a row says which counter spoke it, and from 1.19 the two disagree by one, so the distinction matters where before it did not. The only discriminator is the metronome's own stroke words: a guided track carries two of them on every rep -- 'Down' and 'Up' on vertical work, 'Drive' and 'Return' on horizontal -- so a track carrying rep calls and no stroke word came from the unguided counter, whose whole vocabulary is bare digits, 'Rep N', 'Last rep' and 'Done'. 'Hold' is NOT one of those words and must not be read as one: it is a pause the prescription asked for, absent from every tempo without a mid-rep pause, and it is also the word a timed HOLD set's prep speaks. Two rows may carry the same instant, and that is NOT a duplicate: the guide merges a rep call into a stroke's own word and speaks them as one utterance ('Down, Rep 3'), because the speech engine cancels whatever it was saying when a new utterance arrives. Both words were said, so both are written, at one clock reading taken once -- the stroke word first, the call second. Consumers matching a stroke row still match it unchanged; the call is a row beside it, never a suffix on it. What this array is NOT: a record of the reps performed. It is what the app SAID, on the metronome's own schedule, whether or not the lifter followed it -- repMarks is what was counted. Sets recorded before the app wrote the merged call carry the stroke word alone, and nothing in the row distinguishes a set that spoke no call from one that spoke it and did not write it down. A track may also end on `Set ended`, which is NOT the same ending as `Done`: `Done` means the prescription was called all the way through, `Set ended` means the guide never called `Done`: the lifter stopped a guided set early -- the failure tile, or the early exit offered during the lead-in -- or the set had no rep target for the guide to finish, in which case it is an ordinary completion. It is NOT on its own evidence that a set was failed; read `failed` for that. Both are spoken aloud and both bound the set's rep list at their own instant; a reader wanting the moment a set was called over should look for either. From 1.16 every guided set carries exactly one of the two. A guided set whose track carries neither was recorded before 1.16. On those, a track ending on a stroke means the guide never called `Done` and the app wrote no terminal word -- the lifter ended the set early, or the set had no rep target for the guide to finish. The record cannot tell those two apart; read `failed` and `reps` against the prescription.

t_ms.description: Epoch milliseconds when the cue was spoken.

repMarks.description: The instants a rep was COUNTED during this set, epoch milliseconds on the same clock as the raw IMU, heart-rate and cue streams. Detailed export only, the same terms voiceCues is published on. What was counted, never what the bar did: a mark is written when the lifter taps the rep button or when the voice guide calls a rep, so on a straight-rep set carrying no tempo these are the only per-rep instants anywhere in this document -- repMetrics entries carry durations and an ordinal position and no clock, and voiceCues is what the app SAID rather than what was counted. Absent rather than empty, and the absence is weak: a sensor-counted set produces no marks at all, and neither does any set recorded before the app stored them, and nothing here tells those two apart; neither is evidence that no rep was performed. The number of marks may disagree with reps, in both directions -- a rest-screen correction rewrites reps and cannot reach a mark already written, and the guide calls a rep on its own schedule whether or not the lifter followed it. Where they disagree, reps is what the set was recorded as and this is what was counted while it happened.

items.description: Epoch milliseconds at which a rep was counted.

romSpread_pct.description: How far the reps of this set disagree with each other about rom_m: the population standard deviation as a percentage of meanRom_m. A machine has one travel and a lifter range of motion varies a little, so a large value says the displacements the set derived channels rest on do not agree with each other. ABSENT, never 0, when the set segmented fewer than two reps, or when the reps average no displacement at all - dispersion is undefined there and a number would be a claim about evidence that does not exist. Published at n=2, where it is real but weak; read it against the rep count. WHAT IT CANNOT TELL YOU: it does not separate a segmenter that mismeasured a good set from a lifter whose range genuinely varied, and if a capture ever shows high spread with segmentation known to be correct then this figure is decoration rather than diagnosis. The seated leg curl rail, whose travel is fixed at 0.4-0.5 m, is where to test that.

peakPower_w.description: Best instantaneous concentric (drive) power across the set, watts.

meanConPower_w.description: Mean of per-rep average concentric power, watts.

noRepsReason.description: Why this set resolved no reps - schema 1.18. The one key in this object written when every other key is absent, and the only thing separating a set whose velocity reconstruction ran away from a manual set recorded with no sensor at all: both otherwise publish reps: [], summary: {} and no velocityLossBasis. Each value names WHICH GATE of the segmenter emptied the rep list and claims nothing about the bar or the lifter. afterSetEndCue: reps were resolved and the set's own end cue excluded all of them, so segmentation did not fail. noMovement: no sample left the pause band. runsExceedDisplacementCap: more than half the set's movement runs displaced further than any real phase can, which the DSP reads as unanchored integration drift. runsBelowStartThreshold: no movement run survived demotion, and at least as many failed on peak speed as on duration - a tie is included here and reads as too slow. runsTooBrief: no movement run survived demotion, and more of them failed on duration than on peak speed. phasesUnpaired: runs survived and none paired into a rep. driveBelowMinRom: every drive the pairing walk reached fell under the minimum range of motion - on a concentric-first lift the drive alone is the rep, so no pair need have been formed. ABSENT ON A SET THAT RESOLVED ANY REP AT ALL, including one that resolved 1 of 10 performed - its absence is not a statement that the reps are right. Absent too on every set recorded before 1.18: the value is frozen into the stored analysis when the set is recorded and nothing re-runs the segmenter at export time.

duration_s.description: Hold/carry seconds recorded for timed sets. Since 1.13 a timed set ends when its clock reaches the seconds the set was WORKING TO -- plannedDuration_s unless the lifter changed the hold in the change-set dialog, in which case theirs -- so this equals plannedDuration_s only on a set that ran to its target AND was not changed by the lifter; a set the lifter ended by hand carries what it actually lasted, and a set the lifter corrected afterwards on the rest screen carries the corrected figure. Corrected and measured seconds are NOT distinguishable here: reps publish repsManual and there is no counterpart for duration. FROM 1.18 THIS KEY IS ABSENT on a set that ended before its work phase began; such a set carries `abandonedInPrep` instead. Before 1.18 it published 0 there, and that 0 was never a measurement. A set recorded before database v15 carries no answer either way and publishes this key exactly as it always did.

abandonedInPrep.description: True when the set ENDED BEFORE ITS WORK PHASE BEGAN -- the lifter's tap started the recording, the lead-in was still running, and the set was over before the clock or the cadence started (1.18, #216). It is a statement about the CAPTURE and not about the lifter: the same write path is taken by a set abandoned during its lead-in for any reason, including a slot the app should not have armed at all. What follows from it: `duration_s` and `prep_s` are absent because neither was measured, `reps` is 0 because nothing was counted rather than because nothing was lifted, and any `failed` on such a set is the app's derivation -- read `failedByLifter` to confirm. The raw stream is still real and still worth reading; what it captured is a lead-in. OMITTED WHEN FALSE, and omission is NOT proof of the opposite: whether the work began is a database column added at v15, so every set recorded before it carries no answer and publishes nothing here. A missing key means "the work began, or the app could not tell".

side.description: Unilateral sets: the arm the set WORKED. Since 1.17 (#215) this is the lifter's own statement where they made one on the change-next-set control, and the plan's prescription otherwise; read it against `plannedSide` beside it, and where the two differ the lifter swapped arm order. BEFORE 1.17 this key was a copy of the plan's own declaration -- the app had nowhere to record a worked side -- so on an older document it says what was PRESCRIBED and is silent about what was worked, and a reader who took it for either was right only by accident.

plannedSide.description: Unilateral sets: the arm the PLAN prescribed, frozen when the set was recorded (1.17, #215). ABSENT, never null and never a copy of `side`, on bilateral work, on an ad-hoc set and on a set the lifter appended -- none of those was prescribed a side -- and on every set recorded before database v14, where the column did not exist. So absence does NOT mean the lifter worked what was asked: it means nothing asked, or the set predates the pair. Nothing backfills it, because on those older rows `side` WAS the prescription and copying it across would assert that the app knew which limb moved.

rpe.description: PER-SET RPE on a 1-10 scale: how much THIS ONE SET had left in it. Logged when the set ends; correctable afterward on the rest screen. ONE QUESTION, ANCHORED IN TWO UNITS, because the resolution a lifter can supply changes with the distance from failure. Since 1.14 the app's grid offers exactly seven rungs: 10 nothing left, 9 one rep left, 8 two reps left, 7 three reps left -- reps-in-reserve, in that movement's own words on a hold or an explosive lift -- then three HEADROOM rungs, whose captions are authored per unit and never converted: on a rep set 6 'could have added 10-15 lb' or 'could have added 5 kg', 4 '20-30 lb' or '10 kg', 1 'much more'; on a hold or a carry the same three rungs ask in seconds, 6 'could have gone 15-30 s longer', 4 'about a minute longer', 1 'much longer'. The pound band spans two equipment increments, 10 lb on a bar and 15 lb on a stack, because the app has no declared increment anywhere and cannot know which is in front of the lifter -- so the tile names a WEIGHT and never a notch. THIS EXPORT DOES NOT RECORD which unit's caption was on screen for a given set, nor whether the set drew the load or the time rungs; read the session's own unit and the set's `duration_s` if that matters. The figures in seconds are authored rather than measured; the pound and kilogram bands come from the equipment the lifter actually meets. 2, 3 and 5 are valid values carrying no tile: the gaps exist so the anchors sort, and a value there is a real point on the same ruler rather than corrupt data. WHAT A PRE-1.14 VALUE MEANT: the grid then offered 6 to 10 only and 6 was its floor, 'easy, 4+ reps left', absorbing everything 1 and 4 now take; 7 through 10 are unchanged. Nothing rewrites stored values. THIS IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT FROM THE SESSION-LEVEL `sessionRpe`, which is the lifter's 1-10 answer for the whole workout; the two ranges are now identical and the two must never be averaged or compared as one quantity.

failed.description: True when the set is marked failed: the lifter tapped it as failed, the set fell short of its planned reps or duration and the app derived a failure, or both. The derived case needs no lifter input at all. WHICH OF THE TWO a given set carries is `failedByLifter`, from 1.18; without it a tapped failure and a derived one are indistinguishable here.

failedByLifter.description: Whether the LIFTER called this set failed, rather than the app deriving it from a shortfall (1.18, #216, #169). Present only beside `failed`, and a `false` is a real statement rather than a gap: the set failed, the app derived it -- short of its prescribed reps or seconds, or ended during its lead-in -- and the lifter never said so. ABSENT on every set that did not fail, and on every set recorded before database v15, where the tap lived in the rest screen's memory for the life of that screen and was discarded; nothing backfills it, because there is no source to backfill from. A correction on the rest screen moves it with `failed`: re-tapping the effort or correcting a miscounted rep total rewrites both together, so the pair cannot disagree.

limiter.description: WHY THE SET ENDED, in the lifter's own answer rather than the app's derivation. A CLOSED vocabulary, because grouping failures by reason is the only thing this field is for; the lifter's free words are a separate key, limiterNote, and never a value here. muscle: the target muscle reached its limit, so the load is at the edge -- a progression signal. grip: a different limiter entirely; the back had more and the hands did not, so train grip rather than dropping the main load. form: could have continued and should not have -- usually reduce load or volume, which is the OPPOSITE read from muscle. pace: the prescribed tempo got away, or fatigue arrived early; on a programme that prescribes tempo this is directly actionable. slip: technical or equipment, not capacity. setup: the set was set up wrong before it was ever a test of the muscle -- a bad body position, a seat or a pin at the wrong height, the wrong grip taken -- and the lifter corrects it next session at the SAME load. Its own answer and not a shade of form or slip, because the three carry three different prescriptions: form is form degrading UNDER load and reads as reduce the load, slip is something going wrong mid-set, and this is an error made before the first rep. So this set's numbers are a reading of the set-up and NOT a capacity reading: do not read the shortfall as a ceiling, and do not drop the load for it. Distinct from outside in that the set is the lifter's own to correct rather than an interruption with no training content (#146). pain: pain, or something felt wrong. NEVER a progression signal and the one a coach most needs to see -- it is grouped apart from the performance answers on the page for that reason and should be read apart here too. outside: the set was interrupted -- someone needed the rack, the phone rang. NOT a training signal at all, and the value is that analysis can discard such a set rather than read it as capacity; without it, the app's rule that every unfinished set is a fail would silently depress the record. other: none of the above, with the words in limiterNote. ASKED OF FAILED SETS AND OF COMPLETED SETS RATED AT THE COUNTED END (#191): a set the lifter rated rpe 7 through 10 and finished is asked the same question and stores the same answer, so a set carrying this key did NOT necessarily fail -- read `failed` for that, never the presence of this key. A completed set rated in the headroom rungs (rpe 1, 4, 6) is not asked, because the rung already says there was room left. A completed set rated 2, 3 or 5 -- values the column holds but no tile offers -- and a completed set with no rating at all are not asked either. On such a set the answer names what LIMITED the set rather than what ended it; muscle then reads as the muscle being the limit rather than as failure, and the same for grip, form and pace. OMITTED WHEN THERE IS NO ANSWER, and omission is not an answer of its own: the page is skippable in one tap, a whole class of set is never asked, and every set recorded before database v13 carries nothing. A missing key means 'skipped, never asked, or recorded before the app could ask' -- never 'ended for an unknown reason', and it must not be counted as a category.

limiterNote.description: The lifter's own words, present only beside an answer, and in every export this app has written, only where `limiter` is `other`. Published VERBATIM, with one exception the lifter can see: the characters shown in the field as they type are the characters stored, except that a leading or trailing space is trimmed once when the note is saved. What is stored is exactly what appears here and in the raw archive's meta.json. Capped at 120 characters, which the app truncates at rather than rejecting. It carries no line breaks, no double quote and no backslash: the quote and the backslash are dropped as the lifter types and a line break becomes a space, because the raw archive's set manifest is assembled as text and escapes nothing, so a note containing one would make that whole document unparseable for every set in the session. Absent where there is no answer at all, absent where `other` was tapped and no words were typed, and absent for every answer other than `other` in anything this app writes -- the publish gate refuses an orphaned note rather than re-deciding which answers may carry one, so that a row written by a later build has its words published beside its answer rather than silently deleted.

warmup.description: True when this set was PREPARATORY -- a ramp set, a warm-up, work that is not the training stimulus. It is a statement about what the set was FOR and carries no claim about `rpe`: since 1.14 a warm-up set is rated on the same scale as any other set and usually is, so do NOT exclude these sets from effort analysis on the strength of this flag. Excluding them from volume or progression is a different question and the flag still supports it. TWO PRODUCERS since 1.14, and `warmupByLifter` says which one a given set carries: the plan declares it, through the plan-schema 1.9 key of the same name, and the lifter may mark or unmark the set afterwards on the rest screen. WHERE THE TWO DISAGREE the lifter's mark wins, because the plan's declaration is a prediction written before the session and the mark is a statement by the person who did the set. Where `warmupByLifter` is present the plan's own declaration is NOT published and cannot be recovered from this document; the app's row keeps both. Before 1.14 the only producer was an effort TILE, and tapping it stored this flag together with a null `rpe`; on a session recorded before that version, `warmup: true` with no `rpe` means the app could not record both, not that the lifter declined to rate the set. OMITTED WHEN FALSE, and omission is not proof of the opposite: a set nobody declared and nobody marked publishes no `warmup` even if it was a ramp.

warmupByLifter.description: True when the LIFTER stated this set's purpose themselves rather than leaving the plan's declaration to stand. It says which fact `warmup` carries and changes nothing about what `warmup` means. Present with `warmup` ABSENT is a real statement and not a contradiction: the lifter said this set was NOT a warm-up, which on a set the plan declared as one is a deliberate override. OMITTED WHEN FALSE, which covers every set the lifter never marked and every set recorded before database v13; absence is therefore 'the plan's word, or nothing', never 'the lifter said no'.

added.description: True when the LIFTER appended this set to the exercise mid-session and the plan did not prescribe it. Adherence is read from plannedReps beside reps, and from how many sets an exercise carries against how many the plan asked for; an appended set occupying a prescribed slot corrupts both readings at once, because it inflates the count AND -- having no prescription of its own -- publishes no plannedReps either, so it would otherwise read as a prescribed set whose prescription went missing. An appended set publishes no plannedLoad_kg, plannedReps or plannedDuration_s, and that absence is a statement rather than a gap: nothing prescribed it. It DOES publish tempoPrescribed, rest_s and plannedPrep_s: none of the three is cleared for an appended set, so each carries whatever the exercise block already gave every other set in it, tempo adjusted by anything the lifter has stated since. tempoPrescribed on any set names the tempo the set RAN rather than a frozen prescription, so on an appended set it names a tempo nothing prescribed for that occurrence. Its load_kg, reps and hold are what the lifter was standing on when they added it -- the corrected load, not the plan's. OMITTED WHEN FALSE, and omission is not proof of the opposite on an older document: the flag is a database column added at v12, so every set recorded before it reads false and an appended set on such a session is indistinguishable from a prescribed one. A missing key means "prescribed, or recorded before the app could tell". Placement, for a reader reconstructing the session's order: an appended set is queued AFTER the exercise's remaining prescribed sets, so it appears last within its exercise block rather than next after the set that prompted it.

voided.description: True when the LIFTER says they did not perform this recorded set. The set is still here and so is everything it always carried: its load, its reps or hold, its prescription, its summary and its raw streams in the companion archive are exactly as they were recorded, and this key is what says they must not be read as work that happened. A voided set must be dropped from volume, from a set count and from any progression read; its figures describe a row, not a performance. PUBLISHED RATHER THAN WITHHELD, on purpose: removing the set would make this document disagree with the app's own history and would make a set that was recorded and not performed indistinguishable from one that was never recorded. NOT DERIVED, EVER -- the app cannot tell a set that did not happen from one that failed instantly, and neither can a reader: a 0-second failed timed set is the shape of a fabricated row AND the shape of an unrack-and-fail. Only the lifter's own mark appears here, and nothing backfills it. OMITTED WHEN FALSE, and omission is not proof of the opposite on an older document: the flag is a database column added at database v16, so every set recorded before it reads false and a set an older build recorded that the lifter never performed is indistinguishable from one they did. A missing key means "performed, or recorded before the app could ask". Reversible: un-voiding clears this key and voidReason together.

voidReason.description: The lifter's own words for why the set was not performed, present only on a voided set. Beside the mark and never inside it, the way limiterNote sits beside limiter: a reader grouping unperformed sets needs a boolean to filter on, and free text in that position would destroy exactly that grouping. Absent on a voided set the lifter had nothing to add about, which is the ordinary case, and cleared when a set is un-voided, so it never survives beside a set the lifter says they DID perform. It carries no line breaks, no double quote and no backslash, for limiterNote's reason: the raw archive's set manifest is assembled as text and escapes nothing.

repsManual.description: True when reps were entered or corrected manually rather than sensor-counted.

repMetricsComplete.description: False when the sensor segmenter resolved a different number of reps than the set records — fewer, or more, than the lifter or the voice guide counted. Everything derived from the segmented reps is then drawn from a sample of the set rather than from the set: velocityLoss_pct, tempoCompliance, summary, and the repMetrics array where one is present. Read false as a caveat on those figures whether or not per-rep detail was requested. True is weaker than it looks: when repsManual is false the recorded count IS the segmenter's count, so the two agree by construction and this says nothing independent. Absent means the segmenter resolved no reps at all, which is a third state and not a synonym for false — nothing derived from reps is published either, so there is no figure left to qualify.

setSensors.description: How many accelerometers this set was armed with, which roles they carried, which of those reached the raw archive, which one the set's figures were computed from, whether that was the role the set armed, and what stopped a second stream where two units were PAIRED. What is armed is decided by the hardware ALONE since 1.15 -- which units the app has been paired with, and how the lifter has labelled them: no plan and no in-app setting asks for a count, so there is no planned figure to publish beside the actual one. Nothing here counts files, and a reader must not either. `count`, `expected` and `shortfall` are declarations made when the set began; `present`, `analysedRole` and `analysedFellBack` are observations of which units streamed, decided when the set was RECORDED. Absent on the ordinary one-sensor set -- one bar sensor that delivered -- which is what keeps a single-sensor export identical to what earlier versions wrote; since 1.17's fifth change a one-sensor set whose only unit was SILENT does publish this object, with `count` 1, both role lists empty and `soleSilent` carrying what the app could see of that link; absent therefore covers both a set recorded with one bar sensor and a set recorded before the app could capture two, and does not distinguish them, exactly as an absent `geometry` does not. A role is the identity of a PHYSICAL UNIT and asserts nothing about which end of a bar or which hand it was on -- units get swapped and are corrected in post-processing, so the export deliberately makes no anatomical claim. Do not read a role as `side`, which is a different fact about which limb was worked.

count.description: How many sensors the set was actually armed with. A `plannedCount` stood in front of this key until 1.15 and is gone with the declaration it read. NOT the length of `expected`, and the difference is the interesting case: a set that met two PAIRED units it could not tell apart records count 1 with an EMPTY `expected`, because its single stream carries no role and inventing one would label a capture nobody labelled. `shortfall` says which case that is.

expected.description: The roles this set was armed for, in order. ALWAYS WRITTEN when this object is, INCLUDING EMPTY: an empty list means the set's streams carry no role -- which is what a set that met two paired units it could not tell apart looks like, see `shortfall` -- and that is a statement, not an absence. The roles that are MISSING are the set difference against `present`; there is no third key for them, because a duplicate statement of one fact is one that can disagree with its own inputs.

present.description: The roles whose stream reached the raw archive, in the order of `expected`. REACHING THE ARCHIVE IS NOT BEING ANALYSED: one frame is a file, so since #209 a role here may be one that delivered too few frames to analyse and that the app therefore moved the analysis off -- read `analysedFellBack` for whether it moved, and `silent` for what the app could see of that unit's link. One of three observations in this object, beside `analysedRole` and `analysedFellBack`; `count`, `expected` and `shortfall` are declarations made when the set began. It is stated rather than left to be inferred because this document lists no filenames, so a reader holding only session.json could not otherwise tell a captured role from a missing one. ALWAYS WRITTEN when this object is, INCLUDING EMPTY, and must never read as 'not stated'. An empty list means one of two things and `expected` is what separates them: with a NON-EMPTY `expected` it is a set whose every armed unit went silent, which is the most informative state here; with an EMPTY `expected` it is a set whose single stream carries no role, so there was never a role that could appear here -- read `shortfall` and `soleSilent` for what that set was. That second reading is not new: a set that met two paired units it could not tell apart has always published both lists empty.

analysedRole.description: Which role's stream every figure in this set was computed from -- summary, repMetrics, velocityLoss_pct, tempoCompliance, all of it. Since #207, widened by #209, it is a role that delivered ENOUGH FRAMES TO ANALYSE wherever one did -- the boundary is when the set was RECORDED, not what the document's `schemaVersion` says: a set armed to analyse a unit that delivered too few frames to analyse is analysed from the unit that delivered enough, and `analysedFellBack` is what says the app moved. Read that key rather than comparing this one with `present`, which no longer separates the two cases. It can still name a role absent from `present` in three situations, and none of them is a set whose figures came from a surviving unit: a set where NOTHING streamed, whose summary is empty because there was no capture at all; a set whose armed unit delivered NOTHING while the only unit that did stream delivered too few frames to analyse, where the analysis stayed on the armed role and `present` is NOT empty -- the archive holds that partner's file, no stream reached the analysis, and the summary is empty anyway; and a set recorded by a build that predates this key, whatever the document's `schemaVersion` says -- such a build pointed the analysis at the armed unit whatever happened and published nothing derived when that unit was silent. Absent when no role was in play.

analysedFellBack.description: True when `analysedRole` is NOT the role the set was armed to analyse: that unit delivered too few frames to analyse, another one delivered enough, and the figures come from the one that did (1.17, issue #207; widened from "no stream at all" to "too few frames to analyse" by issue #209). ABSENT means `analysedRole` is the role the set was armed to analyse -- the app did not move it. It does NOT say that unit delivered: a set where NOTHING streamed carries no flag either, and its summary is empty. Read `present` for which units reached the archive and this key only for whether the analysis moved. Absent is also what every set recorded by a build that predates this key carries, whatever the document's `schemaVersion` says -- the flag is frozen into the set's row when the set is RECORDED and only copied out at export -- and it means the same thing there: no earlier build could move the analysed role. It is written only when true, the same way `failed` and `warmup` are, because false is the unremarkable normal and omission reads correctly. It is NOT derivable from the other keys: wherever some unit delivered enough frames to analyse, the analysed role appears in `present` whether or not it moved; and where no unit did, the analysis stayed on the armed unit and did not move at all, whatever `present` holds -- so the comparison separates nothing either way. A set that fell back is a set recorded with one usable accelerometer out of two armed; treat its figures as single-sensor figures from the named role. DO NOT read `expected` against `present` to find the unit it moved off: since #209 the unit it moved off may appear in `present`, because a unit that delivered a handful of frames put a file in the archive and still delivered too few frames to analyse. This key is the only thing that says the analysis moved, and no key here says how many frames any unit sent.

shortfall.description: Why two or more PAIRED units produced one stream, absent when nothing was in the way. "rolesUnassigned": at least one paired unit carried no A/B label. "rolesCollide": every paired unit is labelled and two of them share a label. PAIRED IS NOT CONNECTED, and this key says the weaker of the two things: the app never opened a link to a second unit in this state, and it decides from a persisted list of units it REMEMBERS, so a shortfall says two units are paired and cannot be told apart -- NOT that both were switched on, in range, or anywhere near the gym. In either case the app recorded ONE stream rather than guessing, because two 20-byte WitMotion frames carry no checksum and interleaving two streams it cannot tell apart fabricates plausible samples instead of failing. Absent on a dual set, and absent on the ordinary one-sensor set where this whole object is absent too. It exists because "there was one sensor" and "there were two and one was unusable" are different facts about a session, and since 1.15 removed plannedCount nothing else here separates them. THIS DESCRIBES THE DEVICE ROSTER, NOT THE SET, so expect it on every set of a session rather than on the sets something went wrong on: one stale paired unit left over from an old sensor is enough to write it on every row until the lifter forgets that unit, and reading a session of them as a session of separate incidents is the wrong reading. It is written per set anyway, because the alternative -- writing it once, or not at all when it never changes -- makes a session recorded ENTIRELY under an unusable pair indistinguishable from one recorded with a single sensor, which is the distinction this key exists for. One exception, and it is historical: a set recorded before 1.15 under a plan declaring two sensors stored the reason as a `plannedCount` of 2 beside a `count` of 1 rather than as a word, and the build that writes this document does not read that key. Such a set therefore publishes `count` 1 with an empty `expected` and NO shortfall, and the reason it recorded one stream is not recoverable from this document. A reader meeting `count` 1 with an empty `expected`, no shortfall AND no `soleSilent` is looking at one of those sets, not at a set where nothing was in the way. The `soleSilent` qualifier is load-bearing since 1.17's fifth change: a set armed with one bar sensor that delivered nothing now publishes this same shape and is not one of those rows.

silent.description: Which ARMED units delivered too few frames to analyse across this whole set, keyed by role, with a word for what the app could see of each one's link at the moment the set ended (1.17, issue #213; widened from "nothing at all" by issue #209). The boundary is the analysis's own: a unit under it produced a capture no summary could be computed from, and since #209 a role named here may still have a file in the raw archive, because one frame is a file. ABSENT means every armed unit delivered a stream the analysis could run on -- or that the document was written by a build that could not observe delivery at all, which is every set recorded before this version, and that absence is correct rather than a default. Absence has two further meanings this version cannot remove. On a set shorter than three seconds, an armed unit whose last frame arrived during the preceding rest reads as delivering and is left out. And a set armed with one bar sensor arms no ROLE at all, so this object is absent there and `soleSilent` carries the same word for that set without one (#224) -- the two are never both written. The ROLE is a key and NOT a second statement of which units were missing. It was `expected` minus `present` until #209, which a reader could compute; it is now `expected` minus the units that delivered enough to analyse, which a reader holding only this document CANNOT compute, because no key here publishes a frame count. A duplicate list would be one that can disagree with its own inputs, which is what `expected` says about itself for the same reason. What is new is the WORD, and every word here is WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS. "notLinked": no usable GATT link was up at that moment. It is a MERGE and cannot be read as a diagnosis -- nothing in this app reads the operating system's bond state, so a unit that was switched off, out of range, never bonded, whose bond was removed in the phone's Bluetooth settings behind the app's back, or that the phone's own adapter refused, or one that connected and then failed service discovery, all arrive here as the same word. "linkWithoutSensor": a device answered, GATT service discovery succeeded, and it exposed no notify characteristic this app can read -- so something is paired under that role that is not a bar sensor this app understands. "linkedSilent": the link was up and the app had subscribed for notifications, and nothing came down it. THIS IS THE ONE A CONNECTED INDICATOR CANNOT EXPRESS, and it is what a set that reads as paired throughout while recording nothing looks like. It does NOT prove the subscription succeeded: the app publishes its connected state as soon as the notification descriptor write is issued and never observes the result, so a peripheral that rejected the subscription is indistinguishable here from one that accepted it and then went quiet. "tooSoon": the LINK had been armed for less than the window the app waits before it is willing to say a unit is silent, so nothing was concluded -- a real third answer, not a soft "no". The window is counted from the instant the app last DELIBERATELY pointed that link at a device -- a floor on the arming, not the arming: it starts at the app's own start instant and the reconnect loop can re-point without moving it -- bounded by the set's own start, and NOT from the length of the set alone: a two-second set on a unit that has been up all session and delivered nothing reads "linkedSilent" here, because the floor this window is measured from is never later than the set's own start, so the age tested is the LARGER of the set's own duration and the time since that link was armed. "tooSoon" therefore needs BOTH at once -- a set shorter than three seconds AND an end LESS THAN three seconds after that link's arming -- reaching either alone answers something stronger (1.17, #225). EVERY VALUE HERE IS AN OBSERVATION OF A LINK, NEVER OF THE HARDWARE. No claim is made about a battery, a mounting, or what the lifter did. The window is a fixed three seconds ending at the moment the set ended, not the set itself: on a set shorter than that the reading can be driven by a frame that arrived before the set began. It is the same FUNCTION the READY and rest screens ask, not the same reading: those are asked at a different INSTANT, the moment the screen drew, so the screen and the row can differ about one unit. The grace floor is the same fact on both sides since 1.17 -- the instant the app last DELIBERATELY pointed that link at a device, a floor on the arming and not the arming: it starts at the app's own start instant and the reconnect loop can re-point without moving it -- except that the row's is additionally bounded by the set's own start, so the two can still differ about a link armed DURING the set. The row is written only where that unit delivered too few frames to analyse, empty or otherwise.

soleSilent.description: What the app could see of the ONE armed link on a set whose single stream carries NO ROLE, absent when that link delivered a stream the analysis could run on (1.17, issue #224; the bar moved from "any frames at all" to "enough frames to analyse" by issue #209). This is `silent`'s answer for the set that has no key to hang it off. A role exists only where two paired units carry two different labels, so a set armed with one bar sensor -- the ordinary configuration -- has a structurally empty `silent`, and until this key a whole session recorded through a paired unit whose link delivered nothing published nothing whatever about it. A WORD rather than a one-entry object: there is no role to key it by, and a key invented for the purpose would put something that reads like a role into a document whose readers are told a role is the identity of a physical unit. IT IS NEVER WRITTEN BESIDE `silent`; the two are one fact in two vocabularies and a set carries at most one of them. It appears on three shapes of set, all of which record one unroled stream through the one link the app holds: a set armed with a single paired unit; a set that met two paired units it could not tell apart, which keeps its `shortfall` beside this, because that describes the device ROSTER before the set and this describes the LINK during it; and a set whose two paired units ARE labelled apart but whose preferred address names neither of them, which carries no `shortfall` at all -- the roster is not what is wrong, the preference is. Both publish `count` 1 with an EMPTY `expected` and an EMPTY `present`, because the stream carries no role and inventing one would label a capture nobody labelled. THE VOCABULARY IS `silent`'s AND EVERY WORD IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS; read that key's description for each limit in full. In short: "notLinked" is a MERGE -- nothing in this app reads the operating system's bond state, so switched off, out of range, never bonded, a bond removed in the phone's settings behind the app's back, an adapter that refused, and a connect that failed service discovery all arrive as that one word. "linkWithoutSensor": a device answered and exposed no notify characteristic this app can read. "linkedSilent": the link was up and subscribed and nothing came down it -- the state a connected indicator cannot express, and it does not prove the subscription succeeded. "tooSoon": the LINK had been armed for less than the window the app waits before it is willing to say a unit is silent, so nothing was concluded -- counted from the instant the app last DELIBERATELY pointed that link at a device -- a floor on the arming, not the arming: it starts at the app's own start instant and the reconnect loop can re-point without moving it -- and not from the length of the set alone: the floor is never later than the set's own start, so BOTH the set's own duration and the time since that link's arming must be under the window, exactly as `silent` describes it (1.17, #225). EVERY VALUE IS AN OBSERVATION OF A LINK, NEVER OF THE HARDWARE: no claim is made about a battery, a mounting, or what the lifter did. ABSENT means the set captured a stream the analysis could run on from that one link -- at least enough frames to analyse -- or, on a set shorter than the window, that its last frame arrived during the preceding rest and read as delivering -- or that the document was written by a build that could not observe an unroled link at all, which is every set recorded before this version, and that absence is correct rather than a default. A link that fed enough of a set to analyse and then went silent also publishes nothing here; one that sent one to seven frames and stopped IS named here. It is the same FUNCTION the READY and rest screens ask, not the same reading: those are asked at a different INSTANT, the moment the screen drew, so the screen and the row can differ about one unit. The grace floor is the same fact on both sides since 1.17 -- the instant the app last DELIBERATELY pointed that link at a device, a floor on the arming and not the arming: it starts at the app's own start instant and the reconnect loop can re-point without moving it -- except that the row's is additionally bounded by the set's own start, so the two can still differ about a link armed DURING the set. The row is written only where that unit delivered too few frames to analyse, empty or otherwise.

geometry.description: How the lift moved and how the sensor was mounted for this set, AS THE APP RESOLVED IT — not as a plan declared it, because a declaration may have been overridden by the app's precedence chain and an ad-hoc set has no plan at all. This is what makes the rest of the set checkable: tempoPrescribed is POSITIONAL notation (digit 1 = the down stroke, digit 3 = the up stroke), so which stroke is the eccentric follows from `concentric` and `plane`, not from the digit order — on a leg curl or a pushdown the down stroke is the concentric. Without this object, tempoCompliance is a verdict whose input the reader cannot see. Absent means the set was recorded before the app stored this; absent must NOT be read as vertical/drive-up/sensor-on-the-bar, because a wrong declaration is worse than none. Present means all nine keys are present: the object is written whole or not at all, including the booleans when they are false.

startsWith.description: Which phase opened every rep of this set. A squat starts eccentric; a deadlift or a press from the rack starts concentric.

concentric.description: Which way the driving phase moved. 'down' for leg curls, lat pulldowns and pushdowns. Independent of startsWith, and it is what decides which tempo digit is the eccentric on vertical work.

plane.description: The plane the LIFTER moved in. On 'horizontal' there is no up or down, so the tempo digits revert to the classic phase reading: digit 1 = eccentric, digit 3 = concentric. This is the lifter's plane, not necessarily the sensor's — see sensorOnStack.

sensorOnStack.description: True when the sensor rode a cable weight stack. The stack travels VERTICALLY however the lifter moves, so this overrides `plane` for the axis that was actually measured: a seated row with this true is a vertical measurement of a horizontal exercise.

sensorInverted.description: True when the sensor moved OPPOSITE to the load the lifter drove — the usual case with a sensor on a cable stack. Measured motion was flipped back into the lifter's frame before analysis.

travelRatio.description: Lifter-side travel per unit of sensor travel; 1 for a direct mount, 2 for a 2:1 pulley. Every velocity and rom_m in this set is LIFTER-side, so on a 2:1 pulley they are twice what the sensor saw. Published alongside sensorInverted because the two are one multiplier: reading either alone gives the wrong scale.

kind.description: How the movement is performed. Decides whether a tempo applies at all, whether peak rather than mean velocity is the headline, and whether the set is measured on the clock.

bodyweight.description: True when the lifter's own body was the load. load_kg then INCLUDES body weight, and as of schema 1.5 plannedLoad_kg is paired on the same scale — the plan's declared added load plus the same body weight — so the two remain directly comparable on such a set.

geometrySource.description: Where each resolvable geometry value came from, so a guess is not read as a declaration. 'declared' = a plan stated it; 'seeded' = the app's built-in definition of a lift it ships; 'inferred' = guessed by matching words in the exercise id, which gets ordinary names wrong; 'default' = nothing supplied it and no inference for that value exists, so the type default stood. NOTE the ONE value missing here: sensorInverted carries no source. Plan schema 1.12 widened its plan key to nullable, so a declared false and an omitted key are two distinct states there now and it could carry a source the way the seven published values do; none is published because that would add a required key here for a value no consumer reads. sensorOnStack was a second of them until schema 1.17: its plan key is nullable now, so an omitted key on one of the machines the app ships a mount for reads 'seeded' here. bodyweight was a third until schema 1.19: its plan key is nullable too, since #227 made it so after this text was first written, so a declared false and an omitted key are now distinguishable the way sensorOnStack's pair is, and this document now reads a declared false as 'declared' too, since schema 1.19 (#220). It reads 'seeded' when the app's own definition of the lift is body-weight work and no plan declared anything, and 'default' only when nothing was declared and nothing was seeded; it never reads 'inferred', because the id is matched exactly against a table rather than read for words.

bottomPause_s.description: Seconds the bar was still at the BOTTOM turnaround of this rep, measured between this rep's own two detected movement phases. ABSENT, never zero, when the rep has no bottom turnaround inside it: on a lift whose reps start at the bottom the bottom is the rep's BOUNDARY, and the stillness there runs on until the next drive begins, so it holds the lifter's rest and cannot be separated from a hold. Also absent on a rep the segmenter counted from the drive alone, which resolved one phase and therefore has no turnaround. Exactly one of bottomPause_s and topPause_s is present on a rep that resolved both its phases, and it is the same one for every rep of a given lift. THE FIGURE IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE SEGMENTATION: it is bounded by the two phases this rep resolved, so where reps were merged it covers everything between them -- 14.27 s on one committed leg-press capture that resolved 2 detections for 8 performed reps. Read it beside repMetrics length against reps.

topPause_s.description: Seconds the bar was still at the TOP turnaround of this rep, on exactly the rule bottomPause_s states, with top and bottom exchanged.

peakPower_w.description: Peak instantaneous power during this rep's concentric, watts.

meanConPower_w.description: Average power over the concentric phase of this rep, watts.
